Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR ports Agents and Memory settings rendering from Lit to Solid while retaining synchronous state and Gateway mutation owners. **Example:** Edit AGENTS.md under Settings > Agents > main > Files. - **Before:** Lit renders the editor, preview, and save controls. - **After:** Solid renders those controls using the existing file-editing owner. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Strong visual evidence supports the migration, but the repeated locale defect and removed reset assertion prevent approval. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (screenshot): Prepared before/after screenshots exercise the built Control UI's migrated Channels, Automations, and Files rendering with synthetic fixtures across desktop/mobile light/dark profiles; inspected layouts are consistent, and the later fixture and adapter changes do not invalidate that visual evidence. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Agents settings remain on the older renderer during the Control UI's directed Solid migration. **Reason:** The recorded migration direction supports this focused surface conversion, and retaining the existing domain owners limits behavioral churn. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 4 items remain** Keep open: this useful, maintainer-directed migration still has the previously reported locale regression and lost model-picker reset assertion. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `f6a8b50105a4b9a2711838e3669dd96dc9e3b20c` ## Before merge - [ ] **Subscribe the Agents header to locale changes (P2)** - Changing locale while Agents remains mounted leaves its title and subtitle in the previous language. Both route helpers use imperative t from i18n/index.ts, so these JSX expressions acquire no locale dependency; replacing OpenClawLightDomElement also removes its I18nController refresh. Use the existing reactive translation projection for both labels and cover a locale change without remounting. This repeats the unresolved prior finding. - [ ] **Retain the model-picker reset assertion on agent switches (P2)** - The migrated test removes the assertion that switching from alpha to beta replaces the primary model picker. Its remaining selected-label assertion can pass while a reused picker retains open/search state from the previous agent, the distinct lifecycle contract repaired in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72328. The production keyed boundary remains present, but losing it would now escape this regression test. Restore the reset assertion, consistent with the Solid migration policy to preserve assertions when replacing a harness. This repeats the unresolved prior finding. - [ ] **Complete next step** - Resolve the GitHub-reported merge conflicts while preserving the Solid cutover and current main's changes. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of Live locale refresh** - deb7faf7b0668d3bc01161aff4fba0a85a65829c: Shared Lit bases subscribe to locale changes so mounted pages refresh without remounting. ## Findings - [P2] Subscribe the Agents header to locale changes — `ui/src/pages/agents/view.tsx:101-103` - [P2] Retain the model-picker reset assertion on agent switches — `ui/src/pages/agents/view.test.tsx:343-347` ### Provenance - `Live locale refresh` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (deb7faf7b0668d3bc01161aff4fba0a85a65829c: Shared Lit bases subscribe to locale changes so mounted pages refresh without remounting.) ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Retain the agent-switch reset assertion and cover a locale change while the Agents header remains mounted; neither scenario is established by the inspected screenshots.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Control UI receives agent selections, configuration, and Gateway snapshots, renders settings panels, and dispatches edits through existing capability owners. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Settings navigation] --> B[Solid bridge] B --> C[Agents and Memory state owners] C --> D[Reactive projections] D --> E[Solid settings panels] E --> F[Existing capability operations] F --> G[Gateway] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Complete the Solid cutover while preserving live locale updates, agent-switch control resets, and existing mutation ownership. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes that changing locale while Agents stays mounted cannot invalidate its imperative header translations; no runtime reproduction was run under the read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The migration appropriately retains synchronous domain owners and canonical interop adapters, but must preserve the locale subscription and reset coverage it replaces. Full review comments: - [P2] Subscribe the Agents header to locale changes — `ui/src/pages/agents/view.tsx:101-103` Changing locale while Agents remains mounted leaves its title and subtitle in the previous language. Both route helpers use imperative t from i18n/index.ts, so these JSX expressions acquire no locale dependency; replacing OpenClawLightDomElement also removes its I18nController refresh. Use the existing reactive translation projection for both labels and cover a locale change without remounting. This repeats the unresolved prior finding. Confidence: 0.99 - [P2] Retain the model-picker reset assertion on agent switches — `ui/src/pages/agents/view.test.tsx:343-347` The migrated test removes the assertion that switching from alpha to beta replaces the primary model picker. Its remaining selected-label assertion can pass while a reused picker retains open/search state from the previous agent, the distinct lifecycle contract repaired in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72328. The production keyed boundary remains present, but losing it would now escape this regression test. Restore the reset assertion, consistent with the Solid migration policy to preserve assertions when replacing a harness. This repeats the unresolved prior finding. Confidence: 0.96 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.97 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.
